nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
Can't export D-FINE to onnx when setting dynamo=True. I have slightly modified the export script from the D-FINE repo to export with dynamo=True
    torch.onnx.export(
        model,
        (data, size),
        output_file,
        input_names=["images", "orig_target_sizes"],
        output_names=["labels", "boxes", "scores"],
#        dynamic_axes=dynamic_axes,
        opset_version=16,
        verbose=False,
        do_constant_folding=True,
        dynamo=True,
        report=True,
    )
See generated report:
report.txt
Here's how I tested
cd /
git clone https://github.com/Peterande/D-FINE
cd /D-FINE
pip3 install -r requirements.txt
pip3 install onnxsim onnxscript
mkdir -p models
cd models
wget -q https://github.com/Peterande/storage/releases/download/dfinev1.0/dfine_s_obj365.pth
wget -q https://github.com/Peterande/D-FINE/blob/master/configs/dfine/objects365/dfine_hgnetv2_s_obj365.yml
sed -i 's|data = torch.rand(32, 3, 640, 640)|data = torch.rand(1, 3, 640, 640)|g' /D-FINE/tools/deployment/export_onnx.py
sed -i 's|dynamic_axes=dynamic_axes|dynamo=True|g' /D-FINE/tools/deployment/export_onnx.py
python3 /D-FINE/tools/deployment/export_onnx.py -c /D-FINE/configs/dfine/objects365/dfine_hgnetv2_s_obj365.yml -r /D-FINE/models/dfine_s_obj365.pth

nodes.bodyText:
I am fine tuning llm model with fsdp parallel training. My training was running without any issue 3 days ago ( 28th August). Since 30th August I am getting OOM with the same training code.
I verified other libraries that I use - their version are the same. Only difference pythorch nightly release is from 30th of August.
Training is on B200 Machine with 178.9GB gpu memory, on 28th August and before gpu memory usage was around ~166GB and from 30th of August it is ~177GB approaching 100% and eventually failing with OOM.
I am wondering was there any change that caused fsdp performance degrade?
-- I am using nightly release because of flash attention-2 compatibility
cc @H-Huang @awgu @wanchaol @fegin @fduwjj @wz337 @wconstab @d4l3k @pragupta @ezyang

        model_output += new_text
    thread.join()'''

    time_start = time.time()
    outputs = model.generate(
        inputs,
        max_new_tokens=max_length,
        #max_length = 1000,
        #eos_token_id=terminators,
        do_sample=do_sample, 
        temperature=temperature,
        top_p=0.9,
        num_beams=num_beams
    )
    time_end = start = time.time()

    batch_size = inputs.shape[0]
    res_text = []
    num_out_tokens = 0
    num_input_tokens = 0
    for batch_idx in range(batch_size):
        res_tokens = outputs[batch_idx][inputs.shape[-1]:]
        res_text.append(tokenizer.decode(res_tokens, skip_special_tokens=True))

        #adjust the stats for total number of generated tokens
        num_out_tokens += len(tokenizer.encode(res_text[-1])) #note that we reencode the response text to avoid counting pad tokens
        num_input_tokens += inputs.shape[-1] #this is not exactly accurate as pad tokens are counted
    run_time = time_end - time_start
    stats = {'num_output_tokens' : num_out_tokens, 'num_input_tokens' : num_input_tokens, "run_time" : run_time}

    # print(textwrap.fill(res, width=100))
    return res_text, stats


def main():
    #load configs
    config_file = open('./config.json')
    configs = json.load(config_file)
 
    #set the device
    device = "xpu" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "cpu"

    #BitsAndBytes can be used to further quantize the model (post training quantization)
    bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(**configs['bnb_config'])
    model, tokenizer = model_load(configs["model_id"], configs["ACCESS_TOKEN"], bnb_config, device)
    model.generation_config.cache_implementation = configs["cache_implementation"]
    if configs["torch.compile"]:
        #compile forward model of LLM
        model.forward = torch.compile(model.forward, mode="reduce-overhead", fullgraph=True)

    global PAD_TOKEN 
    PAD_TOKEN = tokenizer.eos_token_id


    #load the train split of a "mlabonne/guanaco-llama2-1k" dataset from HF
    dataset_name = configs["dataset_name"]
    ds = load_dataset(dataset_name, split="train")
    preprocessed_dataset_name = dataset_name.split("/")[-1]+"_dataset_preprocessed"
    ds = preprocess_dataset(ds=ds, tokenizer=tokenizer, preprocessed_dataset_name = preprocessed_dataset_name)

    #initialize a data loader
    batch_size = configs["batch_size"]
    dataloader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(ds, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True, num_workers=0, collate_fn=custom_collate)

    running_stats = {'num_output_tokens' : 0, 'num_input_tokens' : 0, "run_time" : 0.0}

    #iterate over dataloader
    for batch_Idx, data_batch in enumerate(dataloader):

        #LLM call
        response, stats = get_response(model, tokenizer, data_batch['inputs'], device, max_length=configs["max_length"], do_sample=configs["do_sample"], num_beams=configs["num_beams"])

        #accumulate stats
        for key in running_stats.keys():
            running_stats[key] += stats[key]
        #print results
        for batch_element in range(batch_size):
            print("SYSTEM: %s" %data_batch['context'][batch_element])
            print("USER:   %s" %data_batch['question'][batch_element])
            print("ANSWER: %s" %response[batch_element])

        print(running_stats)
        print("LLM token throughput is %e tokens/second" %(running_stats['num_output_tokens']/running_stats['run_time']))
        stop = True

nodes.bodyText:
📚 The doc issue
If you look at the docs for PrepareModuleInput, as well as the type hints in the actual PyTorch codebase, you'll notice that the type for input_layouts and desired_input_layouts are specified as Optional[Union[Placement, tuple[Optional[Placement]]]].
The issue is in the tuple[Optional[Placement]] section. Unlike lists, type hints for tuples regulate the number of elements passed in as well as the type of the elements. From the examples section, it is obvious that the intent of this argument is for it to be a tuple containing any number of Optional[Placement] values, but tuple[Optional[Placement]] means "a tuple containing exactly one Optional[Placement].
This is both confusing to read, because it directly contradicts the example code given, and irritating for people using type checkers, since it correctly notices that passing (Shard(0), None) is incorrect for tuple[Optional[Placement]].
Suggest a potential alternative/fix
The correct type for these arguments would be Optional[Union[Placement, tuple[Optional[Placement], ...]]], meaning a tuple with any number of Optional[Placement] elements.
cc @H-Huang @awgu @wanchaol @fegin @fduwjj @wz337 @wconstab @d4l3k @pragupta @ezyang

🐛 Describe the bug
When applying logsumexp over a particular dimension, non-finite values can result in nan gradients even if they do not contribute to the final scalar on which .backward is called. I cannot see a reason for why this ought to be the expected behaviour. Sorry if it is.
import torch


x = torch.tensor([[1., 2., -torch.inf], [2., 1., -torch.inf]])
t = torch.tensor(1., dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True)
y = torch.logsumexp(x / t, dim=0)
print(f"{y=}")

z = y[y.isfinite()].mean() # All non-finite values excluded in the calculation of z
z.backward()
print(f"{t.grad=}")

t.grad = None
y2 = torch.logsumexp(x[:, :2] / t, dim=0) # If non-finite values are excluded before logsumexp, all works fine
print(f"{y2=}")
z2 = y2[y2.isfinite()].mean()
z2.backward()
print(f"{t.grad=}")
Results in
y=tensor([2.3133, 2.3133,   -inf], grad_fn=<LogsumexpBackward0>)
t.grad=tensor(nan)

🐛 Describe the bug
🐛 Describe the bug
The docstring example in scaled_dot_product_attention contains a redundant and ineffective dtype conversion.
Code location:
torch/nn/functional.py - in the docstring of scaled_dot_product_attention

  
    
      pytorch/torch/nn/functional.py
    
    
        Lines 5821 to 5826
      in
      3d40642
    
  
  
    

        
          
                       attn_bias = torch.zeros(L, S, dtype=query.dtype, device=query.device) 
        

        
          
                       if is_causal: 
        

        
          
                           assert attn_mask is None 
        

        
          
                           temp_mask = torch.ones(L, S, dtype=torch.bool).tril(diagonal=0) 
        

        
          
                           attn_bias.masked_fill_(temp_mask.logical_not(), float("-inf")) 
        

        
          
                           attn_bias.to(query.dtype) 
        
    
  


Issue:
attn_bias = torch.zeros(L, S, dtype=query.dtype, device=query.device)  # Already query.dtype
if is_causal:
    # ...
    attn_bias.masked_fill_(temp_mask.logical_not(), float("-inf"))
    attn_bias.to(query.dtype)  # Redundant! Already query.dtype, and result not assigned
Problems:

attn_bias is already created with dtype=query.dtype
masked_fill_ is an in-place operation that doesn't change dtype
attn_bias.to(query.dtype) is redundant since it's already the correct dtype
The result of .to() is not assigned back, making it completely ineffective

Expected fix:
Remove the line attn_bias.to(query.dtype) entirely.

🐛 Describe the bug
I think I might be getting this wrong, but reporting just in case.
The code below is a simple reproducer that would produce a graph break in the absence of set_fullgraph(False). I expect set_fullgraph to split the graph into two parts (y := x + 10 and f.x - y), but once a graph break occurs, the frame is skipped and the code runs on eager.
import torch

@torch.compile(backend="eager", fullgraph=True)
def fn(x):
    y = x + 10

    with torch._dynamo.set_fullgraph(False):
        class Foo:
            def __init__(self, x):
                self.x = x

    f = Foo(x)
    return f.x - y

x = torch.tensor([1.0])
y = fn(x)
print(y)
It looks like it is missing a @break_graph_if_unsupported in the LOAD_BUILD_CLASS opcode?
Versions
PyTorch main branch

Summary
Summarizing and adding some data to comments @zou3519  made to me.
TLDR is that B200 memory throughput is lower than expected for elementwise ops like copy_
Updated we have a script
benchmark the memory throughput of a cat function in pytorch
import torch
import triton

for dtype in [torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32]:
    element_size = dtype.itemsize

    input1 = torch.zeros((128 // element_size) * 1024, 1024, device="cuda", dtype=dtype) # 128 MiB data
    input2 = torch.zeros((128 // element_size) * 1024, 1024, device="cuda", dtype=dtype) # 128 MiB data
    output = torch.zeros((128 // element_size) * 1024, 2048, device="cuda", dtype=dtype) # 256 MiB data

    torch.cat([input1, input2], dim=1, out=output) # 512 MiB IO

    output = triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(lambda: torch.cat([input1, input2], dim=1, out=output), rep=100)

    bdwidth = 512 / output * 1000 / 1000 / 1000 # TiB/s

    print("\t".join([str(dtype), f"{output:.2f} ms", f"{bdwidth:.2f} TiB/s"]))

nodes.title: Some transformers `export / compile` tests fails (`Aborted (core dumped)`) with `torch 2.9 nightly` but pass with `torch 2.8`

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
To Reproduce
Running on A10
1. Install torch 2.9 nightly build:

python3 -m pip uninstall -y torch torchvision torchaudio && python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir -U --pre torch torchvision torchaudio torchcodec --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cu126

2. Install transformers

git clone https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git && cd transformers && git fetch origin && git checkout 242bb2cafccec9f90479f5f688bca9d240b1031f && pip install -e .[torch,testing]

3. Running test
RUN_SLOW=1 python3 -m pytest -v tests/models/beit/test_image_processing_beit.py::BeitImageProcessingTest::test_can_compile_fast_image_processor

RUN_SLOW=1 python3 -m pytest -v tests/models/vit/test_image_processing_vit.py::ViTImageProcessingTest::test_can_compile_fast_image_processor


RUN_SLOW=1 python3 -m pytest -v tests/models/video_llava/test_video_processing_video_llava.py::VideoLlavaVideoProcessingTest::test_can_compile_fast_video_processor

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
Hi,
I'm not sure if this is a bug, but it seems more apt to make this an issue.
I’ve been using torch.utils.data.DataLoader with torchvision.datasets.CocoDetection and noticed that the first-batch latency (time to fetch the first batch) is unreasonably high on Windows, regardless of the size of the dataset. While this overhead is small relative to the total training time, it becomes noticeable during development: for example, when making small code changes and repeatedly waiting for the first batch to load. In that context, reducing first-batch latency can be quite useful.
After profiling, I found that the biggest bottleneck is pickling. To address this, I implemented __getstate__ and __setstate__ methods in ModifiedCocoDetection to avoid pickling coco object. Then, I benchmarked first-batch latency for two datasets (small and large), varying both batch_size and num_workers. This plot visualizes the ratio of modified/original latency:

The results show that for num_workers > 1, the modified version is consistently faster.
One of the puzzling behaviours is that the effect of avoiding pickle is smaller for larger dataset, as it seems logical for larger dataset to be more advantageous as pickling large objects is much more expensive. Also, for num_workers=1, large dataset is slower..
Is this behaviour expected? If so, are there any side-effects?
I attached the raw measurements in csv format.
large.csv small.csv
Below is the minimum reproducible benchmark code (you need to replace YOUR_ROOT, YOUR_ANNFILE):
import time

from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from torchvision.datasets import CocoDetection
from torchvision.transforms import v2 as T


def collate_fn(batch):
    return tuple(zip(*batch))


class ModifiedCocoDetection(CocoDetection):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.annFile = kwargs["annFile"]

    def __getstate__(self):
        state = self.__dict__.copy()
        del state["coco"]
        return state

    def __setstate__(self, state):
        from pycocotools.coco import COCO

        self.__dict__.update(state)
        self.coco = COCO(self.annFile)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import pandas as pd
    train_root = YOUR_ROOT
    train_annFile = YOUR_ANNFILE

    transforms = T.Compose(
        [
            T.Resize(256),
            T.ToImage(),
        ]
    )
    train = CocoDetection(
        root=train_root,
        annFile=train_annFile,
        transforms=transforms,
    )
    modified_train = ModifiedCocoDetection(
        root=train_root,
        annFile=train_annFile,
        transforms=transforms,
    )
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        columns=["batch_size", "num_workers", "first_batch_latency", "modified_first_batch_latency"]
    )

    for batch_size in [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]:
        for num_workers in [0, 1, 2, 4, 8]:
            dl_kwargs = {
                "batch_size": batch_size,
                "num_workers": num_workers,
                "collate_fn": collate_fn,
            }
            if num_workers > 0:
                dl_kwargs["multiprocessing_context"] = "spawn"

            start = time.perf_counter()
            train_loader = DataLoader(train, **dl_kwargs)
            next(iter(train_loader))
            end = time.perf_counter()
            train_time = end - start
            del train_loader

            start = time.perf_counter()
            modified_train_loader = DataLoader(modified_train, **dl_kwargs)
            next(iter(modified_train_loader))
            end = time.perf_counter()
            modified_train_time = end - start
            del modified_train_loader

            df.loc[len(df)] = [batch_size, num_workers, train_time, modified_train_time]

    df.to_csv("coco_time.csv", index=False)

🐛 Describe the bug
flex attention is slower than sdpa
import time
import statistics
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

from torch.nn.attention.flex_attention import flex_attention, create_block_mask

B = 2
H = 32
L = 4096
D_head = 128
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

WARMUP = 10
ITERS = 50

torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False

torch._dynamo.config.cache_size_limit = 512
torch._dynamo.config.accumulated_cache_size_limit = 4096

try:
    flex_attention = torch.compile(flex_attention)
except Exception as e:
    print("torch.compile(flex_attention) failed or not necessary:", e)


def causal_mask(b, h, q_idx, kv_idx):
    return q_idx >= kv_idx


torch.manual_seed(0)
q = torch.randn(B, H, L, D_head, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
k = torch.randn(B, H, L, D_head, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
v = torch.randn(B, H, L, D_head, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)

block_mask = create_block_mask(
    causal_mask, B=None, H=None, Q_LEN=L, KV_LEN=L, device=device, _compile=True
)


def call_flex(q, k, v, block_mask):
    return flex_attention(q, k, v, block_mask=block_mask)


def call_sdpa(q, k, v):
    return F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True)


def benchmark(fn, name, warmup=WARMUP, iters=ITERS, use_block_mask=False):
    device_is_cuda = device.startswith("cuda")
    if device_is_cuda:
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats(device)

    for i in range(warmup):
        out = fn(q, k, v, block_mask) if use_block_mask else fn(q, k, v)
        if device_is_cuda:
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
    times = []
    for i in range(iters):
        if device_is_cuda:
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        out = fn(q, k, v, block_mask) if use_block_mask else fn(q, k, v)
        if device_is_cuda:
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
        t1 = time.perf_counter()
        times.append(t1 - t0)

    avg = statistics.mean(times)
    med = statistics.median(times)
    stdev = statistics.stdev(times) if len(times) > 1 else 0.0
    mn = min(times)
    mx = max(times)
    # throughput: tokens/sec = B * L / avg_time
    toks_per_sec = (B * L) / avg if avg > 0 else float("inf")

    peak_mem_gb = None
    if device_is_cuda:
        peak_bytes = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(device)
        peak_mem_gb = peak_bytes / (1024**3)

    results = {
        "name": name,
        "avg_s": avg,
        "med_s": med,
        "stdev_s": stdev,
        "min_s": mn,
        "max_s": mx,
        "tokens_per_sec": toks_per_sec,
        "peak_mem_gb": peak_mem_gb,
    }
    return results


def main():
    print(f"Device: {device}  B={B} H={H} L={L} D_head={D_head}")
    results = []
    try:
        print("Benchmarking flex_attention ...")
        r = benchmark(call_flex, "flex_attention", use_block_mask=True)
        results.append(r)
    except Exception as e:
        print("flex_attention benchmark failed:", e)

    try:
        print("Benchmarking scaled_dot_product_attention (SDPA) ...")
        r = benchmark(call_sdpa, "scaled_dot_product_attention")
        results.append(r)
    except Exception as e:
        print("SDPA benchmark failed:", e)

    print("\n--- Results ---")
    for r in results:
        print(f"{r['name']}:")
        print(f"  avg time     : {r['avg_s'] * 1000:.3f} ms")
        print(f"  median time  : {r['med_s'] * 1000:.3f} ms")
        print(f"  stdev        : {r['stdev_s'] * 1000:.3f} ms")
        print(
            f"  min / max    : {r['min_s'] * 1000:.3f} ms / {r['max_s'] * 1000:.3f} ms"
        )
        print(
            f"  tokens/sec   : {r['tokens_per_sec'] / 1e6:.3f} Mtokens/s ({r['tokens_per_sec']:.0f} toks/s)"
        )
        if r["peak_mem_gb"] is not None:
            print(f"  peak memory  : {r['peak_mem_gb']:.3f} GB")
        print("")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

🐛 Describe the bug
There seems to be an accuracy issue in torch.compile when running meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B with bfloat16.
Things I've tried:

torch.compile backend eager/aot_eager/aot_eager_decomp_partition all work fine, so I guess this is an inductor issue
dtype=float32 works fine too
TORCHINDUCTOR_EMULATE_PRECISION_CASTS=1 does not seem to fix the issue

repro script:
    def test_meta_llama(self):
        from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
        import torch
        import time 
        import copy

        model_name = "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B"
        tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
        model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
            model_name, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cuda"
        )
        model.eval()
        
        model.generation_config.do_sample = False
        model.generation_config.use_cache = True
        model.generation_config.cache_implementation = "static"
        model.generation_config.max_new_tokens = 2000
        model.generation_config.pad_token_id = tokenizer.eos_token_id
        model.generation_config.temperature = 0.0

        vocab_size = tokenizer.vocab_size
        input_ids = torch.randint(
            low=0,
            high=vocab_size,
            size=(1, 1000),
            device="cuda",
            dtype=torch.long,
        )
        example_inputs = {"input_ids": input_ids}

        model_copy = copy.deepcopy(model)

        start = time.time()
        res1 = model_copy(**example_inputs).logits
        print(time.time() - start)

        model_copy = copy.deepcopy(model)
        model_copy.forward = torch.compile(model_copy.forward)

        start = time.time()
        res2 = model_copy(**example_inputs).logits
        print(time.time() - start)
        
        self.assertTrue(torch.allclose(res1, res2, atol=0.001))

from __future__ import annotations
import torch

class MaskedMHA(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, H_q, H_kv, D):
        super().__init__()
        self.H_kv = H_kv
        num_heads_total = H_q + 2 * H_kv
        self.qkv_proj_vid = torch.nn.Linear(H_q*D, num_heads_total*D)
        self.qkv_proj_txt = torch.nn.Linear(H_q*D, num_heads_total*D)
        self.out_proj = torch.nn.Linear(H_q*D, H_q*D)
        self.H_q = H_q
        self.D = D

        
    def forward(self, x_vid, x_txt, attn_mask):
        qkv_vid = self.qkv_proj_vid(x_vid)
        qkv_txt = self.qkv_proj_txt(x_txt)
        qkv_vid = qkv_vid.reshape((*qkv_vid.shape[:-1], -1, self.D))
        qkv_txt = qkv_txt.reshape((*qkv_txt.shape[:-1], -1, self.D))

        
        q_vid = qkv_vid[..., :self.H_q, :]
        k_vid = qkv_vid[..., self.H_q:self.H_q + self.H_kv, :]
        v_vid = qkv_vid[..., self.H_q + self.H_kv:, :]

        q_txt = qkv_txt[..., :self.H_q, :]
        k_txt = qkv_txt[..., self.H_q:self.H_q + self.H_kv, :]
        v_txt = qkv_txt[..., self.H_q + self.H_kv:, :]

        q = torch.cat([q_vid, q_txt], dim=-3)
        k = torch.cat([k_vid, k_txt], dim=-3)
        v = torch.cat([v_vid, v_txt], dim=-3)

        out = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q.transpose(-2,-3), k.transpose(-2,-3), v.transpose(-2,-3), attn_mask=attn_mask, enable_gqa=True)
        out = out.transpose(-2,-3)

        return out

def test_masked_mha(B, H, S, D, device, dtype):
    S_vid = 300
    S_txt = S - S_vid
    print(f"S={S}, S_vid={S_vid}, S_txt={S_txt}")
    x1 = torch.randn(B, S_vid, H*D, requires_grad=True, device=device)
    x2 = torch.randn(B, S_txt, H*D, requires_grad=True, device=device)
    attn_mask = torch.ones(B, 1, S, S, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)

    H_kv = H // 4
    mha = MaskedMHA(H, H_kv, D)
    mha = mha.to(device)
    mha = torch.compile(mha, fullgraph=True, backend="inductor")
    with torch.autocast(device_type="cuda", dtype=dtype, cache_enabled=False):
        out_vid = mha(x1, x2, attn_mask)
        target_vid = torch.randn_like(out_vid)

        loss_vid = (out_vid - target_vid).mean()
        loss = loss_vid
    loss.backward()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    print(f"x1 grad any nan={torch.any(x1.grad.isnan()).item()}")
    print(f"x2 grad any nan={torch.any(x2.grad.isnan()).item()}")
    print(f"loss={loss.item()}")
    for param_idx, param in enumerate(mha.parameters()):
        print(f"{param_idx=} {param.grad.max() if param.grad is not None else None}")


def main():
    B, H, S, D = 2, 32, 549, 128
    device = "cuda"
    dtype = torch.bfloat16
    torch.compiler.reset()
    torch.manual_seed(42)
    test_masked_mha(B, H, S, D, device, dtype)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
In aot_forward_graph, you will see:
view_10: "f32[2, 32, 549, 549][9644832, 301401, 549, 1]cuda:0" = torch.ops.aten.view.default(slice_tensor_2, [2, 32, 549, 549])
but since slice_tensor_2 is legitimately a bf16 tensor, view_10 should be bf16 tensor too. So this f32 dtype annotation seems incorrect. (Note that the Inductor post-grad graph does have the correct dtype annotation.)

nodes.title: Hard error when slicing a tensor with unbacked sizes

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
Description:
When an in-place operation is applied to a non-leaf tensor with requires_grad=True, and the tensor subsequently loses its backward graph node because of Python arithmetic operators, the process’s resident memory keeps growing, indicating a memory leak caused by unreleased reference counts.
To Reproduce
import torch
import unittest
import gc, psutil

def mem_mb_print():
    gc.collect()
    mem = psutil.virtual_memory()
    process = psutil.Process().memory_info().rss

    print(f"used: {mem.used // 1024**1} KB,"
       f"process: {process // 1024**1} KB,"
       f"percent: {mem.percent} %,"
       f"PyTorch tensors: {sum(1 for o in gc.get_objects() if torch.is_tensor(o))}")

class TestLeafGradMaxCUDA(unittest.TestCase):
    @unittest.skipIf(not torch.cuda.is_available(), "CUDA not available")
    def test_cross_grad_max_cuda(self):
        device = torch.device("cuda")

        # leaf GPU tensor
        leaf = torch.randn(8, 1, 24, device=device, requires_grad=True)
        no_leaf= leaf * 1.0

        for _ in range(100):
            window_left = no_leaf[:, :, :-1]          # [8, 1, 23]
            # inplace operators
            no_leaf[:, :, 1:] = torch.max( 
                no_leaf[:, :, 1:],  
                window_left   
            )
            # Python arithmetic operators
            mask = (no_leaf >= 0)
            mem_mb_print()

        loss = mask.sum()

if __name__ == "__main__":
      unittest.main()  

running:
python mem_leak.py
result:

When running the above program, the Python object count and memory usage keep rising after each in-place operation.



However, if I detach the no_leaf tensor before performing the in-place operation, the memory leak does not occur.

        no_leaf= leaf * 1.0
        no_leaf = no_leaf.detach()
        for _ in range(100):
            window_left = no_leaf[:, :, :-1]          # [8, 1, 23]
            # inplace operators
            no_leaf[:, :, 1:] = torch.max( 
                no_leaf[:, :, 1:],  
                window_left   
            )


Versions
Environment:

PyTorch Version: 2.6.0+cu126
OS (e.g., Linux):
